terms.meaning: Information about a page, such as its title, that browsers and search engines read.
A reusable piece of a page that has its own look and behaviour.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the Memory Palace page
sections.what: Brings in the page metadata type and the experience component that the page displays.
sections.why: The page needs these two things to set its title and show the experience.

sections.name: metadata
sections.title: Page title and description
sections.what: Sets the title and short description used in browser tabs and search results.
sections.why: Gives the page a readable name and summary for visitors and search engines.
sections.watch_out: Changing these values changes what browser tabs and search previews show.

sections.name: AtlasPage
sections.title: Page that shows the experience
sections.what: The page's main function. It renders the Memory Palace experience and nothing else.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The thin wrapper appears to be a page shell around the component.

summary: The Memory Palace page: it sets the page title and description and shows the 3D experience as its whole content.
purpose: Gives the Memory Palace its own web address on the site, with a title that browsers and search engines can read.
why: Likely reason: keeps the page file small and puts the real behaviour in the AtlasExperience component. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Step 1 brings in the page metadata type and the experience component. Step 2 sets the title and description. Step 3 renders the experience as the page.
inputs: Nothing from the visitor. The page takes no settings and no query values.
outputs: A full page titled Memory Palace, showing the experience.
risks: Low on its own. Most problems would come from the AtlasExperience component, which is not in this packet.
debug: If the page is blank, check AtlasExperience first. If the browser tab title is wrong, check the metadata block in this file.
